_about: Offline treatment knowledge base for the 38 disease-model classes. Doses are common Indian extension (ICAR / state agricultural university) recommendations for knapsack sprays (per litre of water). Always follow the product label and local KVK advice.

Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple scab
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit; infected fruit cracks and becomes deformed.
Apple___Apple_scab.favoured_by: Cool, wet spring weather; long leaf wetness.
cultural: Rake and destroy fallen leaves after harvest
Prune to open the canopy for air flow
organic: Spray wettable sulphur 2 g/L at green-tip to petal-fall
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Start protective sprays at bud break in wet seasons; repeat every 7-10 days while rain continues.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple black rot
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-edged 'frog-eye' leaf spots, sunken cankers on branches, fruit rot that turns black and mummifies.
Apple___Black_rot.favoured_by: Warm humid weather; dead wood and mummified fruit left in the orchard.
cultural: Remove mummified fruit and dead or cankered branches
Prune in dry weather and burn the prunings
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L at dormancy
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Orchard sanitation is the main control; fungicide covers protect fruit during wet periods.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar apple rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface, later with small tubes on the underside.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.favoured_by: Juniper / cedar trees nearby; wet spring weather.
cultural: Remove juniper or cedar hosts near the orchard where possible
organic: Wettable sulphur 2 g/L from pink bud stage
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Protect from pink bud to 2-3 weeks after petal-fall.

Apple___healthy.name: Healthy apple
advice: No disease seen. Keep the canopy open, remove fallen leaves and fruit, and scout weekly in wet weather for scab and rust spots.

Blueberry___healthy.name: Healthy blueberry
advice: No disease seen. Keep soil acidic and well-mulched, avoid overhead irrigation, and remove dead canes.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.name: Cherry powdery mildew
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on young leaves and shoots; leaves curl and pucker.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.favoured_by: Warm days, cool nights, high humidity; dense canopy.
organic: Wettable sulphur 80 WP 2 g/L (not above 32 °C)
Potassium bicarbonate 5 g/L
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Begin sprays when first white patches appear; repeat after 10-14 days.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.name: Healthy cherry
advice: No disease seen. Keep the canopy open and watch new shoots for white powdery growth in humid weather.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Gray leaf spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey-tan lesions limited by leaf veins; lesions merge and blight leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.favoured_by: Warm, humid weather; continuous maize with crop residue on the surface.
organic: Remove badly infected lower leaves in small plots
chemical: Propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml/L at first lesions before tasselling
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Spray when lesions appear on the third leaf below the ear before silking.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.name: Common rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, raised, cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.favoured_by: Cool (16-23 °C), humid weather with heavy dew.
organic: Usually no treatment needed when only a few pustules are present
chemical: Propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml/L if pustules spread before tasselling
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Scout the upper leaves; spray only if pustules increase quickly before flowering.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Northern leaf blight (Turcicum leaf blight)
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped, grey-green to tan lesions 2-15 cm long, starting on lower leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.favoured_by: Moderate temperatures (18-27 °C) with long dew periods.
organic: Trichoderma-based seed treatment helps reduce early infection
chemical: Mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L at first symptoms
Propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml/L, repeat after 15 days if needed
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Spray when lesions reach the leaves below the ear before tasselling.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.name: Healthy maize
advice: No disease seen. Scout weekly for leaf spots and for fall armyworm damage in the whorl.

Grape___Black_rot.name: Grape black rot
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Tan leaf spots with dark borders and black dots; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.favoured_by: Warm, wet weather from bloom to berry set.
cultural: Remove mummified berries and infected canes
Train vines for good air flow
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L before bloom
chemical: Myclobutanil 10 WP 0.4 g/L from bloom to 4 weeks after
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Critical period is bloom to 4 weeks after; keep fruit covered with protectant sprays in rain.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).name: Esca (black measles)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe yellow / red patches between leaf veins; dark spots on berries; sudden vine collapse.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).favoured_by: Large pruning wounds; older vines; hot weather after rain.
cultural: Prune in dry weather and seal large cuts
Cut out dead wood well below the infected part
organic: Trichoderma paste on pruning wounds
chemical: No curative spray; protect pruning wounds with a recommended fungicide paste (e.g. copper oxychloride paste)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Wound protection at every pruning is the only effective control.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.name: Leaf blight (Isariopsis leaf spot)
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on older leaves, later dry and brittle; early leaf fall.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.favoured_by: Warm, humid weather late in the season.
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Spray at first spots and repeat every 10-15 days in humid weather.

Grape___healthy.name: Healthy grape
advice: No disease seen. Keep the canopy open and scout for downy and powdery mildew after rain.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Citrus greening (Huanglongbing)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).type: bacterial (Candidatus Liberibacter), spread by citrus psyllid
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy, uneven yellow mottling on leaves; small, lopsided, bitter fruit; twig dieback.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).favoured_by: Asian citrus psyllid; infected planting material.
cultural: Remove and destroy infected trees (no cure)
organic: Neem oil 1500 ppm 5 ml/L on new flushes against psyllids
chemical: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL 0.3 ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25 WG 0.3 g/L on new flushes to control psyllids
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: There is no cure. Early removal of infected trees protects the rest of the orchard.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.name: Peach bacterial spot
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular purple-brown leaf spots that fall out ('shot holes'); pitted, cracked fruit.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.favoured_by: Warm rain with wind; sandy soils; susceptible varieties.
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L at leaf fall and bud swell
chemical: Streptocycline 0.1 g/L + Copper oxychloride 2 g/L during wet periods after leaf emergence
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Dormant copper sprays plus protection during wet spring weather.

Peach___healthy.name: Healthy peach
advice: No disease seen. Apply dormant-season sprays as recommended locally and scout leaves after rainy, windy weather.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial leaf spot
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots turning brown with yellow halos; leaves drop; scabby spots on fruit.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.favoured_by: Warm, wet weather; splashing water; infected seed.
cultural: Use disease-free or hot-water treated seed (50 °C, 25 min)
Rotate for 2-3 years away from tomato / chilli
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L
chemical: Streptocycline 0.1 g/L + Copper oxychloride 3 g/L, 2-3 sprays at 10-day intervals
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Start with clean seed and seedlings; remove infected plants early.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.name: Healthy capsicum
advice: No disease seen. Use drip irrigation, keep leaves dry and scout for thrips, mites and leaf spots.

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato early blight
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('target board') on older leaves, often with yellow halos.
Potato___Early_blight.favoured_by: Alternating wet and dry weather; stressed or nutrient-poor plants.
cultural: Balanced fertiliser, especially nitrogen and potash
organic: Trichoderma viride soil application; neem-based sprays slow spread
chemical: Azoxystrobin 23 SC 1 ml/L for heavy attack
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Spray at first symptoms and repeat every 10-15 days.

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato late blight
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked patches on leaves with white mould underneath in humid mornings; tubers rot.
Potato___Late_blight.favoured_by: Cool (10-20 °C), cloudy, humid weather with rain or fog. Spreads very fast.
cultural: Earth up well to protect tubers
Destroy infected haulms; harvest 2 weeks after haulm cutting
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L as protectant
chemical: Mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L as protectant before symptoms
Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP 2.5 g/L or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP 3 g/L once symptoms appear
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Act immediately: it can destroy a field within a week in cool wet weather. Do not use metalaxyl more than 2-3 times per season.

Potato___healthy.name: Healthy potato
advice: No disease seen. In cool, foggy weather apply a protective mancozeb spray and scout every few days for late blight.

Raspberry___healthy.name: Healthy raspberry
advice: No disease seen. Remove old fruiting canes after harvest and keep rows narrow for air flow.

Soybean___healthy.name: Healthy soybean
advice: No disease seen. Scout for rust, yellow mosaic and girdle beetle, and keep the field free of weeds.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery mildew
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery spots on upper leaves that spread to cover the leaf; leaves yellow and dry.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.favoured_by: Dry weather with high humidity; shade; dense planting.
organic: Wettable sulphur 80 WP 2 g/L (not in hot weather on cucurbits; test first)
Potassium bicarbonate 5 g/L
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Spray at first white spots; repeat after 10-15 days.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Leaf scorch
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small, irregular purple spots that merge; leaf edges look burnt and dry.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.favoured_by: Warm, wet weather; old plantings; overhead irrigation.
cultural: Remove and destroy infected leaves after harvest
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 2 g/L
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Spray from early growth in wet seasons; keep foliage dry.

Strawberry___healthy.name: Healthy strawberry
advice: No disease seen. Use mulch to keep fruit off the soil and avoid wetting leaves.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, greasy spots on leaves with yellow halos; raised scabby spots on fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.favoured_by: Warm, wet weather; splashing rain; infected seed and transplants.
cultural: Stake and mulch to reduce splash
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L
chemical: Streptocycline 0.1 g/L + Copper oxychloride 3 g/L, 2-3 sprays at 10-day intervals
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Start sprays early in wet weather; copper alone works poorly once disease is severe.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Early blight
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves; stem lesions near soil; fruit rot at the stem end.
Tomato___Early_blight.favoured_by: Warm, humid weather; plant stress; poor nutrition.
organic: Trichoderma soil application; neem-based sprays slow spread
chemical: Azoxystrobin 23 SC 1 ml/L for heavy attack
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Spray at first spots, repeat every 10-15 days.

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Late blight
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, greasy, dark patches on leaves and stems with white mould underneath; firm brown fruit rot.
Tomato___Late_blight.favoured_by: Cool, wet, foggy weather. Spreads very fast.
cultural: Do not grow next to potato
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L as protectant
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Spray protectively in cool, wet weather; act immediately at first symptoms.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Leaf mould
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with olive-green velvety mould underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.favoured_by: High humidity (above 85%), mostly in polyhouses and dense crops.
cultural: Improve ventilation; reduce humidity in polyhouses
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Keep humidity down; spray at first symptoms.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria leaf spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small, round spots with grey centres and dark borders on lower leaves; tiny black dots in the centre.
cultural: Rotate crops; remove weeds of the same family
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Spray at first spots and repeat every 7-10 days in wet weather.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Two-spotted spider mite
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow speckling on leaves, bronzing, fine webbing on the underside.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.favoured_by: Hot, dry, dusty weather; overuse of pyrethroid insecticides.
cultural: Avoid pyrethroids that kill natural enemies
organic: Neem oil 1500 ppm 5 ml/L
Wettable sulphur 80 WP 3 g/L
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Spray the underside of leaves; rotate miticides.

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Target spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and rings on leaves; sunken spots on fruit.
cultural: Prune lower leaves and improve air flow
organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Spray at first symptoms in humid weather.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upward, small and yellow-edged; plants stunted; few flowers and fruit.
cultural: Remove and destroy infected plants early
organic: Neem oil 1500 ppm 5 ml/L against whiteflies
chemical: No cure for the virus. Control whiteflies: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL 0.3 ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25 WG 0.3 g/L, Spiromesifen 22.9 SC 1 ml/L
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Protect seedlings from whitefly in the first 4-6 weeks.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato mosaic virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern; mottled, fern-like or distorted leaves; uneven fruit ripening.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.favoured_by: Handling plants; infected seed; tobacco use by workers.
cultural: Wash hands and disinfect tools (milk or 10% bleach)
Use certified seed and resistant varieties
organic: No spray cures virus diseases
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Hygiene: avoid touching healthy plants after infected ones; no tobacco near plants.

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy tomato
advice: No disease seen. Stake and mulch plants, water at the base, and scout weekly for leaf spots, whiteflies and mites.
